overview: White fianchettoes the king's bishop to pressure d5 and the long diagonal toward b7. After 4...Be7 5.Nf3 O-O 6.O-O dxc4 7.Qc2 or 6...c6 Black aims for a solid set-up and ...c5 or ...b5. White seeks a small, lasting initiative and the bishop on g2 as a long-term asset without taking risks.

white_ideas.idea: Pressure on the c6/b7 diagonal with Bg2 and Qc2; regain the c4 pawn after ...dxc4.
Slow queenside play with Qc2, Nbd2 and Rd1.

black_ideas.idea: Hold d5 with ...c6 or take on c4 and return it for activity.
Break with ...c5 or ...b5 to free the position and neutralise Bg2.

typical_structures.structure: QGD-type centre with White fianchetto; after ...dxc4 White regains the pawn.

character.notes: Quiet, slow and pressing; little forcing play.

gambit.notes: The c4 pawn comes back, not a gambit.

level.notes: Slow strategic play and subtle move orders.

sublines_that_differ.name: Open Catalan
sublines_that_differ.how: Black takes on c4 and White regains it.

character.reason: Quiet pressure for White with a solid Black set-up; neither extreme.

gambit.reason: Any pawn on c4 comes straight back.

structure.reason: The centre is in tension, as in the QGD.

approach.reason: A mainstream White opening, not a universal system.

level.reason: Plans and move orders matter more than memory.

plans.reason: White's bishop on g2 and a slight edge in space.
